items.title: The Rolling Stones Announce Deluxe Album Foreign Tongues, Loose Lips Featuring Five New Songs
items.summary:
The Rolling Stones will release Foreign Tongues, Loose Lips, an expanded edition of their most recent album, on November 27th through Capitol Records. The package pairs the original record with five recordings pulled from the same sessions that did not make the final track list.

The additions are "Where There's a Will," "Who You Callin' Crazy," "Human Tide," "She Still Comes Around" and "Bad Luck Hideaway." Jazz saxophonist Courtney Pine plays on "Who You Callin' Crazy." "Bad Luck Hideaway" is a vocal duet between Mick Jagger and Keith Richards that had previously circulated only as an iTunes exclusive, making the deluxe set its first wide release.

Consequence reported that pre-orders and pre-saves are open now, with the band offering vinyl, a two-disc CD edition and digital versions. The configuration follows the standard template for catalog expansions of this kind, placing the leftovers alongside the album rather than issuing them separately.

Foreign Tongues arrived earlier with "Mr. Charm" among the songs the band promoted with a video. The group has said it plans to take the album on the road in 2027, which leaves a long runway between the deluxe release and any live performances of the material.

As it stands, the five session tracks represent the only new Rolling Stones music scheduled before that tour, and they arrive attached to the album they were cut for rather than as a standalone release.

items.title: Big Thief Launch Grateful Dead-Inspired Live Archive
items.summary:
Big Thief have opened the Big Thief Live Archive, a free online repository of concert recordings spanning the band's career. The site launches with 10 complete shows, and the group plans to add a new concert on the second Tuesday of every month.

Visitors can browse performances from different eras and build personalized playlists out of their preferred versions of individual songs. To mark the launch, the band shared a live recording of "Incomprehensible" taken from an April performance at Dublin's 3Arena.

The idea came from drummer James Krivchenia, whose interest in the Grateful Dead's vast catalog of live tapes prompted the band to begin recording all of their concerts around 2019, according to Consequence. Front-of-house engineer Alice Wilder and monitor engineer Aleda Deroche captured the early recordings, and 4AD in-house engineer Fabian Prynn handled the mixing.

"Every show we play holds a different energy," the band said in a statement. "The songs are always changing and sound different every night, and we spend so much more time on the road than in studios, and so we felt a desire to create something that captures the ever-undulating aliveness of our music through time."

"Incomprehensible" came out last year on Double Infinity and landed on Consequence's 200 Best Songs of 2025 list. The Dublin version offers a different reading of one of that album's strongest tracks.

The band has already moved on to the next record. In August, Big Thief played their forthcoming triple album Horsepower in full at Nashville's Ryman Auditorium, with Gillian Welch, Iris DeMent and Lucinda Williams joining them onstage.

items.title: Watch Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall’s First Teaser Trailer
items.summary:
The first teaser trailer for Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall arrived today, ahead of the concert film's theatrical run. The clip leans on atmospheric footage and includes a brief passage of "Dead at 23."

The film documents Winter's performance at Carnegie Hall last December, roughly a year after his solo debut Heavy Metal. Janus Films and Criterion are handling distribution, sending the 35mm print on a city-by-city theatrical tour beginning November 20, Pitchfork reported.

The movie follows Live at Carnegie Hall, the album drawn from the same show, which came out last week. Winter is currently on the road with Geese on the band's Getting Killed Again tour.
